meta.title: Improve VM constant folding for OpIn
meta.body_summary: Extend VM constant folding to handle 'OpIn' operations and regenerate all benchmark IR output files.

perf_labels.notes: OpenAI_Codex PR adding constant folding for OpIn; closed by author after ~44h with no reviews or perf evidence beyond IR diff.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 1447 changed lines across 22 files, this is a medium-sized change by absolute volume, but 98% are regenerated benchmark IR outputs (bench/out/*.ir.out). The core optimization in liveness.go adds only 24 lines. As a performance-oriented optimizer extension, it was closed without merge—no review comments and author closed it after ~44 hours, indicating lack of reviewer engagement or incomplete validation.

review_details.concern_detail: No review comments or formal review recorded. The PR was closed by the author with no feedback.
review_details.performance_claim: Extend constant folding to OpIn operations to reduce runtime overhead of membership tests.
review_details.rejection_signals: PR closed by author with no review activity; lack of maintainer engagement likely contributed to closure.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: VM constant folding for a language runtime is a compiler optimization that requires deep integration with existing IR and correctness validation. The agent correctly scoped the change but closure without review suggests maintainers may expect benchmarks or more evidence before accepting such changes.

detection_detail.code_reading: No maintainer code‑reading evidence in dataset; review was never submitted.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: PR body only asks to run `go test` and `mochi-bench`, but provides no benchmark numbers, profiler output, or before/after performance data.

core_change_summary.description: Added constant folding for 'OpIn' instructions in runtime/vm/liveness.go (24 new lines) and regenerated all benchmark IR output files under bench/out/ to reflect the optimization effect.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: Regenerated IR files account for ~98% of total line changes; each file contains updated constant‑folded instruction sequences.
